ai.seo_question: What makes a single passage of Nahj al-Balagha sufficient for spiritual instruction?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī employs this hyperbolic praise to underscore the density of meaning in the sermons, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that views Nahj al-Balagha not merely as rhetoric but as a repository of divine wisdom (hikmah). This statement serves as a meta-commentary on the text's efficacy, asserting that its capacity to provoke spiritual introspection (tafakkur) and guide the perceptive (al-mubṣir) is self-sufficient for moral edification.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If this book had contained nothing save this short utterance it would have sufficed as a successful piece of preaching, a specimen of high philosophy, an object of wisdom for the onlooker and a source of instruction for the meditative watcher.
